title: Amber DNA Extraction & City Biocontamination Simulator
description: A chemistry lab workstation where the user extracts ancient DNA from a mosquito preserved in amber using a multi-step chemical process, then simulates releasing the reconstructed organism into a virtual city to observe biocontamination spread. The user must balance reagent concentrations, maintain temperature equilibria, and can undo/redo extraction steps while monitoring conservation of total molecular mass across all reactions.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing an interactive chemistry lab DNA extraction simulator. Load MosquitoInAmber.glb centered on a lab bench on the left half of the scene and VirtualCity.glb scaled down as a miniature city model under a glass dome on the right half. Use OrbitControls with constrained polar angle. Add three-point lighting plus a warm amber spotlight on the specimen and a cool blue light over the city dome. The interaction flow has 12 steps: (1) Click amber specimen to begin, rotating it under a UV lamp. (2) Use a slider to set solvent concentration (0-100%) which dissolves the amber with a shader-based transparency animation. (3) Pipette reagent A onto the exposed mosquito by clicking a dropper tool. (4) Adjust pH slider (1-14) to activate reagent; only pH 6.5-7.5 succeeds. (5) Apply reagent B via second dropper click. (6) Set centrifuge RPM with a dial widget and click spin to separate DNA. (7) Use a temperature slider to run PCR amplification, keeping 92-96C range. (8) Click to inject amplified DNA into a sequencer panel showing a progress bar. (9) Review extracted genome on a floating holographic display. (10) Click to synthesize organism, spawning a glowing particle above the city. (11) Click the city dome to release, triggering a spreading green contamination wave across VirtualCity using animated shader rings. (12) Use a neutralization button to halt spread. Implement undo/redo buttons that revert any step, restoring previous reagent amounts. Enforce conservation of total molecular mass: display a mass counter that stays constant across all reactions. Each reagent addition subtracts from a finite supply shown in labeled beakers. Invalid parameters flash red warnings. Add a HUD showing current step, mass balance, reagent levels, and undo/redo stack depth.
